tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says the Moroccan dirham is a closed, non-convertible currency. Moroccan Customs tolerates at most 2,000 MAD being carried in or out of Morocco. The Government of Canada says unused dirhams can be converted at the airport exchange counter on departure with proof of your initial currency purchase.

The UK Foreign Office says people posing as official tourist guides commonly harass tourists; if you use a guide in a medina, make sure they have an official badge and permission from the local authority. The Government of Canada advises hiring only official guides recommended by hotels, travel agencies or local tourist authorities.
The UK Foreign Office says that to fly a drone in Morocco you must get permission from the Directorate General for Civil Aviation, or you risk fines and confiscation of your equipment.

During Ramadan the Government of Canada advises refraining in public, between sunrise and sunset, from activities such as drinking, eating and smoking; the UK Foreign Office says doing so in public in the daytime may cause offence.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Morocco?
faq.answer: No. Morocco's Foreign Ministry lists the United States among the countries whose nationals are exempt from an entry visa, but does not state how long the stay may last, and no official source we could read does. The UK Foreign Office says border officials should stamp your passport on entry, and that some travellers without an entry stamp have had difficulties leaving Morocco.

faq.question: How long can EU and UK citizens stay in Morocco?
faq.answer: UK citizens can stay visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism, according to the UK government; to stay longer they must request an extension at a Moroccan police station. EU citizens are also visa-exempt, but Morocco's Foreign Ministry list gives a stay length only for Hungary (90 days), and no other official source we could read states one.

faq.question: Can I buy Moroccan dirhams before my trip?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says the dirham is a closed, non-convertible currency that cannot easily be exchanged outside Morocco, and Moroccan Customs tolerates at most 2,000 MAD being carried in or out. The Government of Canada says unused dirhams can be converted at the airport exchange counter on departure with proof of your initial currency purchase.

faq.question: Who needs Morocco's eVisa and where do you apply?
faq.answer: Many passports, including several Latin American ones (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, Peru), are on the Foreign Ministry's list of nationalities exempt from an entry visa. The eVisa is open to citizens of a listed group of countries — including India, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia, Laos, Brunei, Jordan, Israel, Benin and Guatemala — and to other visa-required travellers who hold a valid multiple-entry non-electronic visa from the US, Schengen, the UK, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Japan, Norway or New Zealand. Apply at the official portal acces-maroc.ma; its eVisa page gives a processing time of 3 business days for the Standard track and 1 business day for Express.

countryFacts.safety.text: Petty crime is common in tourist areas, especially in historical districts (medina quarters) and on beaches. Crimes include: pickpocketing bag-snatching drive-by motorcycle theft of visible jewellery and handbags

It is common for people posing as official tourist guides to harass tourists. If you use a guide in a historical district (medina quarter), make sure they have an official badge and permission from the local authority.
There can be occasional violent crime in Morocco. Criminals have used knives against tourists in street attacks, thefts and burglaries in major cities and along beaches.
avoid quiet areas, particularly after dark
Terrorists are likely to try to carry out attacks in Morocco.
Terrorism attacks could be indiscriminate, including in places visited by foreign nationals

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy season usually extends from November to March, during which flash floods can occur frequently. These can be especially dangerous in the High Atlas valleys.
